name: /work
description: Load context and identify next task

steps.description: Collect coverage, recent memory, pattern hint and local Git once in one Python process; no network or writes.

steps.context: Use release_awareness from the collected command evidence; do not run another checker. This is offline and writes nothing. If disabled, continue quietly; do not enable or check automatically. If there is a notice, summarize it with the configured source and last successful checked_at, keeping stale/unknown separate from current. A fresh update notice offers release notes, remind later or the separately approved update workflow through /updates release. Never invoke check, enable, remind or disable from this read-only command. A previously authorized host entry hook may separately refresh the cache; absent such a hook, the user can explicitly invoke /updates release check. No updater, scheduler, network call or cache write is implied by onboarding or work.

steps.action: Inspect location and the selected task read-only
steps.context: Use the location and task_brief evidence returned by the work collector; do not rerun it. Show the project/location verdict and task ID, revision and requirements-approval state. Git being unavailable in an explicitly non-Git content project means Git status is not applicable; continue brief orientation. Other inspection errors remain unresolved. If selection is missing, stale or conflicting, inspect list/show and ask the owner to select or clear explicitly through /brief-work; /work does not write a selection. Never silently choose a brief.

steps.action: Format and display the work brief
steps.context:
You are producing a work brief to re-orient the user into this project only. Use the collected project-local Git state and TODO before generating the brief. Do not query a cross-project index, hub, vault, or external memory.

Generate a rich, structured brief in this order:

1. RIGHT NOW - reconcile right_now against later events and live Git before describing current state. Quote historical actions as historical; do not promote a completed, cancelled, or rolled-back item into current work. If it contains insufficient recent context, read at most the two newest project-local `.exocortex/events/*.md` files and reconstruct the last work, decisions, next actions, and blockers.

2. SHORT-TERM - summarize shortterm as dated evidence, with source references and unresolved contradictions.

3. SUBCONSCIOUS NUDGE - display subconscious_nudge if non-empty.

4. GIT STATE - use the returned Git status/branch and recent commits. List each modified or untracked path and flag a branch that appears pending integration. A working tree can be shared with another session, so say plainly which listed paths this session did not create; treat every one of them as another writer's work.

5. OPEN ITEMS - read project-local `.exocortex/OPEN_DECISIONS.md` when present and identify unresolved decisions or overdue local actions.

6. NEXT TASK - show the first incomplete task group from the Ready section of `.exocortex/TODO.md`.

Then show the A/B/C choice. Name actual local evidence and identify uncertainty instead of guessing.

If the human chooses B, stage only the paths this session changed, naming each one explicitly. Never run `git add -A` or `git add .`, and never stage a path this session did not create: in a shared working tree that commits another writer's work under this session's name. If ownership of any listed path is unclear, say so and commit nothing until the human resolves it. Offering B is not authority to commit, and it never authorizes push, merge, deployment, or synchronization.
Reuse returned Git and note evidence; do not rerun the helpers or freshness check. Report coverage status, omitted events and truncated excerpts; inspect only source files needed to resolve material uncertainty. Never treat omitted history as reviewed.

If `.exocortex/planning/MASTER_BRIEF.md` exists, read it and its named project-local execution record before recommending the next task. Lead with the overall objective and current slice; check proposed TODO work against the recorded scope and latest approval. Report contradictions or an unavailable known brief instead of treating the newest event as the whole plan. Missing optional briefs are normal. This is read-only context loading, not permission to update the brief or act on its plan.

When a task is selected, read its exact brief with the shared launcher operation `script brief_work.py show <id>`. Lead with its objective and acceptance criteria, compare current artifacts and task-linked events to that revision, and identify the next authorized step. The selected task takes precedence over a generic TODO suggestion; reconcile contradictions with the master brief and current owner instructions. Other-task or older-revision events are historical evidence, not current requirements. For document or content tasks, missing software/Git metadata is not a blocker unless required by the brief. Reading a task, proposed lesson or approval record grants no new authority.
